_note: Timeline beats: what you see or hear at a time, wherever you stand. where: 'open' (any open deck), 'below' (any place under cover), 'any', or a list of place ids. sound (optional): the short cue in sound.js's CUES this beat may play. Source: docs/twenty-boats-research.md section 4.

beats.text: A long grinding shudder runs along the ship's side, then stops.
Word passes along the corridor: the mail room, low down at the front, is flooding. The mail bags are afloat.
Steam is blowing off from the funnels with a roar that drowns out talk.
Seamen are pulling the canvas covers off the lifeboats and clearing the ropes.
At the front end of the corridor, water is creeping up the stairs from the deck below.
The boats are being swung out on their davits until they hang over the side, high above the water.
Stewards come through calling for women and children to go up to the boat deck. Nothing is said about the men.
A rocket goes up from the bridge and bursts high overhead in white stars.
The roar of steam has stopped. In the quiet you can hear voices all along the deck.
The floor slopes down towards the front now, and leans to the left.
An officer calls for all passengers to cross to the right-hand side, to bring her upright.
The band is playing at the top of the Grand Staircase.
The gate at the top of the stairs is open now. First the women were called up; now the stewards let everyone through.
No more rockets go up from the bridge.
Over the rail, the open deck at the front is under the sea. Only the tip of the bow stands clear.
The electric lights are still on, burning steadily.
At the front of the ship, water is coming up the stairways onto the decks.
A crowd is pressing aft, climbing towards the back of the ship as the front goes down.
Towards the front, a funnel tears loose and falls into the sea.
Somewhere in the middle of the ship, a roar of iron parting. The lights are still burning.
